Hi Mia,

Thanks for inviting me to your [[1]] party on Saturday. I'd love to come, but I need to [[2]] my cousin at the airport. Her flight was delayed, so I'm not sure when we'll get back. Could you [[3]] me the address by text? If I arrive late, please don't [[4]] for me before eating. I can [[5]] a sandwich on the way. I hope the weather stays [[6]], since the garden gets muddy after rain.

Best, Sam
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order to make a story. The first one is done for you.
passages.p3:
For centuries, high peaks were commonly treated as dangerous barriers or places inhabited by spirits. During the nineteenth century, however, scientists and artists began to visit them for study and inspiration. Today many people see such landscapes as spaces for recreation, health and self-discovery, rather than territory to be avoided.

Regular visitors often develop a personal bond with a particular ridge, valley or climbing route. They learn where snow lingers, when birds nest and which shelter is safest in a storm. For them, returning year after year is not simply sport; it becomes a form of familiarity with a living place.

Reaching a summit is increasingly documented online. Climbers upload photographs, route maps and altitude records within minutes, allowing friends and strangers to celebrate the result. This habit can inspire others, but it also turns a private expedition into a performance, where visible evidence may matter as much as the climb itself.

After weeks of training, completing a demanding ascent can produce a powerful inner reward. The climber may value this moment even if nobody else knows about it and no official record is set. Unlike prizes gained in competition, the satisfaction comes from overcoming a challenge chosen for oneself.

On crowded routes, some people continue upward despite worsening weather because being able to say they reached the top seems more important than turning back. This attitude has led to avoidable accidents and difficult rescue operations. Experienced guides argue that sound judgement should come before summit claims, especially when conditions become uncertain.

Expeditions to several famous peaks have uncovered a less inspiring reality: campsites littered with oxygen bottles, torn tents and food packaging. In some areas, melting ice has exposed items left decades ago, including personal belongings of climbers who never returned. These findings challenge the romantic image of untouched wilderness.

To reduce long-term harm, park authorities are introducing visitor limits, reusable equipment rules and fees that support trail repair. Some operators now require groups to carry all waste back down and to employ local staff under fair conditions. Such measures aim to protect fragile high-altitude environments while keeping access possible for future generations.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ to need help, just ask the teacher.
questions.explanation:
If' mang nghĩa 'mỗi khi/nếu' nên dùng hiện tại đơn 'happen', không dùng 'would' trong mệnh đề if.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn tình cờ cần giúp đỡ, cứ hỏi cô giáo.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ be rich, but he is not very kind to people.
questions.explanation:
May' diễn tả sự nhượng bộ ('có thể đúng là... nhưng...').
[TD]Dịch: Anh ta có thể giàu, nhưng anh ta không tử tế với mọi người lắm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If only he _____ smoking when the doctor told him, he would be healthy now.
questions.explanation:
If only' + quá khứ hoàn thành 'had given up' diễn tả tiếc nuối về quá khứ, kéo theo kết quả hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: Giá mà anh ấy đã bỏ thuốc khi bác sĩ khuyên, thì bây giờ anh ấy đã khỏe mạnh.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ her assistant of leaking the confidential merger details to a rival firm.
questions.explanation:
Cấu trúc 'accuse sb of + V-ing' (buộc tội ai làm gì) đúng giới từ, khác 'blame sb for'.
[TD]Dịch: Cô ấy buộc tội trợ lý của mình đã làm rò rỉ chi tiết thương vụ sáp nhập mật cho một công ty đối thủ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

It is reported that the old house _____ to a new owner.
questions.explanation:
Bị động hoàn thành 'has been sold' diễn tả việc ngôi nhà đã được bán.
[TD]Dịch: Có tin rằng ngôi nhà cũ đã được bán cho chủ mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

That _____ Tom at the door. He said he would come tonight.
questions.explanation:
Will be' diễn tả sự suy đoán chắc chắn về hiện tại (hẳn là).
[TD]Dịch: Đó hẳn là Tom ở ngoài cửa. Anh ấy nói sẽ đến tối nay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He made the decision without asking anyone, and his team _____ it ever since.
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành 'have regretted' với 'ever since' diễn tả sự tiếc nuối kéo dài từ quá khứ đến nay.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đã quyết định mà không hỏi ai, và đội của anh hối tiếc kể từ đó đến giờ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

In the past, people _____ to bow when they met someone important.
questions.explanation:
Used to' diễn tả phong tục/thói quen từng tồn tại trong quá khứ nay đã mất.
[TD]Dịch: Ngày xưa, mọi người thường cúi chào khi gặp người quan trọng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He arrived _____ for the meeting because his flight had been delayed for hours.
questions.explanation:
Cần tính từ/trạng từ 'late' (muộn); 'lately' nghĩa 'gần đây' nên không hợp ngữ cảnh.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đến muộn cuộc họp vì chuyến bay đã bị hoãn nhiều giờ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ majority of the students passed the test.
questions.explanation:
The majority of' dùng mạo từ xác định 'the' khi nói về đa số một nhóm cụ thể.
[TD]Dịch: Đa số học sinh đã đỗ bài kiểm tra.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ told me you don't eat meat before I cooked dinner!
questions.explanation:
Might have + V3' diễn tả lời trách móc về việc lẽ ra nên làm.
[TD]Dịch: Lẽ ra bạn nên nói cho tôi biết bạn không ăn thịt trước khi tôi nấu bữa tối chứ![/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

We would have been late _____ the taxi driver's fast driving.
questions.explanation:
But for' nghĩa là 'nếu không có', dẫn danh từ để chỉ nguyên nhân giả định.
[TD]Dịch: Chúng tôi đã bị muộn nếu không nhờ tài xế taxi lái nhanh.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ me, I think this movie is not very good.
questions.explanation:
Câu điều kiện thực diễn tả ý kiến hiện tại, dùng hiện tại đơn 'ask' trong mệnh đề if.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn hỏi tôi, tôi nghĩ bộ phim này không hay lắm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You can borrow my flat in Vienna _____ you water the plants and feed the cat.
questions.explanation:
As long as' nêu điều kiện (miễn là), phù hợp ngữ cảnh cho phép có kèm điều kiện.
[TD]Dịch: Bạn có thể mượn căn hộ của tôi ở Vienna miễn là bạn tưới cây và cho mèo ăn.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ you happen to see Lan at school, please give her this book.
questions.explanation:
If + happen to' diễn tả tình huống tình cờ; dùng 'If' cho điều kiện thông thường.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu bạn tình cờ gặp Lan ở trường, hãy đưa cho cô ấy cuốn sách này.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ the bridge been built stronger, it wouldn't be damaged now.
questions.explanation:
Đảo ngữ câu điều kiện: 'Had + chủ ngữ + V3' thay cho 'If... had' diễn tả giả định trái với quá khứ.
[TD]Dịch: Giá như cây cầu được xây chắc hơn, thì bây giờ nó đã không bị hỏng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Direct: 'You shouldn't have spent so much money on that toy.' Reported: Mom told me I _____ so much money on that toy.
questions.explanation:
Shouldn't have + V3' đã ở quá khứ nên giữ nguyên khi tường thuật.
[TD]Dịch: Mẹ nói lẽ ra tôi không nên tiêu nhiều tiền vào món đồ chơi đó.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I found a girl _____ voice is really beautiful.
questions.explanation:
Whose' là đại từ quan hệ chỉ sở hữu, thay cho 'the girl's voice'.
[TD]Dịch: Tôi tìm thấy một cô gái mà giọng hát rất hay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I will lend you my bike _____ that you return it by Friday.
questions.explanation:
On condition (that)' nêu điều kiện ràng buộc (với điều kiện là).
[TD]Dịch: Tôi sẽ cho bạn mượn xe đạp với điều kiện bạn trả lại trước thứ Sáu.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

My friend _____ going to the new restaurant for dinner.
questions.explanation:
Động từ 'suggest' đi với V-ing (không dùng 'suggest sb to do').
[TD]Dịch: Bạn tôi đề nghị đi ăn tối ở nhà hàng mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ have a quick coffee somewhere before catching the late train?
questions.explanation:
Shall we...?' dùng để đưa ra lời đề nghị, rủ rê cùng làm gì đó.
[TD]Dịch: Chúng ta đi uống cà phê nhanh đâu đó trước khi bắt chuyến tàu muộn nhé?[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You look tired!' 'Yes, I _____ for the test since this morning.'
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn 'have been studying' diễn tả hành động kéo dài từ 'since this morning' đến hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: 'Trông cậu mệt quá!' 'Ừ, tớ đã ôn thi từ sáng đến giờ.'[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He was writing his essay when the lights went off, and he realized he _____ to save it.
questions.explanation:
Quá khứ hoàn thành 'had forgotten' diễn tả việc quên xảy ra trước thời điểm mất điện.
[TD]Dịch: Anh ấy đang viết bài luận thì đèn tắt, và anh nhận ra mình đã quên lưu bài.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The plan has been _____ for several weeks.
questions.explanation:
Cụm danh từ 'under consideration' (đang được xem xét) tránh thể bị động.
[TD]Dịch: Kế hoạch đã được xem xét trong vài tuần.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The proposal was _____ rejected by the entire board without further discussion.
questions.explanation:
Trạng từ 'flatly' (thẳng thừng) đi với 'rejected'; 'very/rather' không bổ nghĩa cho động từ kiểu này.
[TD]Dịch: Đề xuất bị cả hội đồng thẳng thừng bác bỏ mà không bàn bạc thêm.[/TD]

The study of the world and how things work
questions.explanation:
science (noun) the study of the world and how things work (môn học nghiên cứu về thế giới tự nhiên và cách mọi thứ vận hành)

for (preposition) showing who is meant to get or use something (dùng để chỉ ra đối tượng hoặc mục đích mà điều gì đó được dành riêng)

Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

What sport do you play most often? Do you prefer playing alone or with other people?
questions.sampleAnswer: I play badminton most often, usually twice a week after work. Although I sometimes practise serves alone, I definitely prefer playing with friends because it is more social, competitive, and motivating. We also encourage each other to improve.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Do you think watching sports on TV is as exciting as watching them live? Why or why not?
questions.sampleAnswer: In my opinion, live sport is more exciting than watching it on TV. In a stadium, you can feel the crowd's energy and celebrate every important moment together. Television is convenient, but it cannot fully recreate that atmosphere.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Some people think school sports make children too competitive. Do you agree? What is your opinion?
questions.sampleAnswer: I do not agree completely. School sports can make some children overly focused on winning, but they also teach teamwork, discipline, and resilience. Teachers should emphasise enjoyment and personal progress, rather than results, so every child feels included.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write a short email to your friend Linh (about 40 to 50 words). Tell her about the Sports Club's campaign, encourage her to join, and mention the benefits of doing sport.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Hi Linh,

Our Sports Club is launching a social media campaign with free trial sessions and student discounts. I think we should join together! Sport is a great way to stay fit, reduce stress and meet new people. The trials are free, so we can try different activities before choosing one. Are you interested?

Best,
Nguyen Minh Anh

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to the Club Manager (about 120 to 150 words). Evaluate the proposed plan, suggest some improvements, and explain how the club can encourage young people to be more active.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Dear Club Manager,

I am writing to comment on the proposed plan to attract more young people to the Sports Club. Overall, I strongly support the social media campaign, free trial sessions and student discounts. These measures could make the club more visible, affordable and less intimidating for students who have not exercised regularly.

To make the campaign more effective, I suggest posting short videos of real young members taking part in classes, team games and fitness challenges. The club could also invite local schools and colleges to share the posts. Free trial sessions should be held at different times, including weekends and evenings, because many students have busy schedules.

In addition, a bring-a-friend scheme or monthly beginner events could help new members feel welcome. Young people are more likely to remain active when sport is enjoyable and social. Regular exercise improves physical health, reduces stress and builds confidence, so this plan could benefit both the club and the local community.

Yours faithfully,
Nguyen Minh Anh

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Can you describe a typical meal in your country? What food do people eat, how is it prepared, and who do you usually eat with?
questions.sampleAnswer: In Vietnam, a typical meal has rice, fish or chicken, vegetables, and soup. My mother often cooks the food by boiling, frying, or steaming it. We put the dishes in the middle of the table and eat together with our family in the evening.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What types of books do people in your country like to read? Why do they like them, and can you give some examples?
questions.sampleAnswer: In Vietnam, many people like reading romance stories, detective books, and books about history. Young people often choose comic books or novels because they are fun and easy to read. My father likes business books, but my sister enjoys Korean romance novels.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What is your favourite time of the day? When is it, what do you do then, and why do you enjoy it?
questions.sampleAnswer: My favourite time of day is early morning, around six o'clock. I usually get up, drink a cup of tea, and listen to music. Then I walk to a small park near my home. I enjoy this time because it is quiet, cool, and peaceful.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: In this picture, four young women are walking together in a shopping mall or on a busy high street. They are probably friends, and they are spending time together after shopping. They are carrying several shopping bags in their hands. Some of the bags are showing famous brand logos. The women are wearing casual and fashionable clothes, such as jeans, jackets, and nice tops. They are smiling and talking, so they are looking very happy and excited. Behind them, there are shop windows with colourful displays. The shops are selling different things, and the area is looking bright and modern. It seems like a pleasant day, and the friends are enjoying their shopping trip.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

What kind of shopping do you enjoy most: online shopping, shopping at a market, or shopping at a mall? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I enjoy shopping at a mall most. I like it because there are many different shops in one place. I can try on clothes before I buy them, and I can see the real colours and sizes. I also enjoy going with my sister or friends. After shopping, we can have a drink or eat something together. It is fun and easy.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Do you think shopping is a good way to spend free time with friends? Why or why not?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think shopping is a good way to spend free time with friends. We can walk around, talk, and look at different shops together. It is also nice to choose clothes or gifts and ask friends for their ideas. However, we should not spend too much money. We can just look at things, have a coffee, and enjoy being together. For me, this is relaxing.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Compare these two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer: In the first picture, I can see three people inside a car. They seem to be friends or family members. One person is driving, and he is looking at the road. The two passengers look comfortable. They are talking together or looking out of the window. In the second picture, there are people on a train or metro. Two people are sitting close to each other, but they do not know each other. One woman is reading a book, while another person is using a phone. There are more passengers behind them. The car is more private because the people know each other. It may also be more comfortable and quiet. However, the train is public, so people usually sit with strangers. In both pictures, people are travelling, but they are doing different activities.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Do you prefer travelling by train or by car?
questions.sampleAnswer: I prefer travelling by car. I usually travel with my family, so a car is good for us. We can talk, listen to music, and stop when we want. It is also easy to carry bags or food. Trains can be fast and cheap, but they are sometimes crowded. Last month, my family and I drove to the beach, and we had a nice trip.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Why do you think many people prefer travelling by train?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think many people like travelling by train because it is easy and safe. They do not need to drive, find a parking place, or pay for petrol. On the train, they can read, sleep, listen to music, or use their phones. Trains are also good for the environment because many people travel together. In big cities, a train can be faster than a car in traffic.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Describe a time when you did something you did not want to do. Say what it was, when it happened, why you had to do it, and how you felt.
questions.sampleAnswer:
One time I did something I did not want to do was last summer. My aunt asked me to look after her small dog for five days. I do not dislike dogs, but I was afraid of them because I had never taken care of one before. I also wanted to stay at home and play games during my holiday.

However, my aunt had to visit my grandmother in another city, and nobody else was free. So I said yes. At first, I felt nervous and a little unhappy. The dog woke up early, and I had to walk it twice a day. It was tiring, especially when it rained.

After two days, I felt better. I learned to give the dog food, play with it, and clean its room. To overcome difficult situations, people can ask family or friends for advice. They can also make a simple plan and do one small thing at a time. I think it is important to sometimes do things we do not enjoy. We can learn new skills, become stronger, and help other people.
